 NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WZTV) — Christa Pike and her legal team are asking a federal judge to order Tennessee to end her isolation in a prison infirmary , arguing the arrangement violates a settlement over her conditions of confinement.
 The emergency motion, filed Friday in Pike’s 2022 federal case, says she has been isolated at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center since returning from the hospital after the state’s failed execution attempt. The filing says she is separated from other inmates and cannot take part in the work, group meals, recreation and supervised activities outlined in a 2024 settlement.
 RELATED COVERAGE | 'Confused and in pain': Christa Pike speaks out for first time on failed execution attempt 
 Pike’s attorneys say they asked the state to house her in a separate area for women receiving temporary medical care, where she could receive treatment and have safe contact with other women. An Oct. 27 email from an assistant attorney general, included with the motion, says the infirmary arrangement serves Pike’s needs as determined by her medical providers and that discussions about long-term housing are premature.
 In a sworn declaration, Pike says she remains physically weak , has wounds on both arms and is receiving wound care, treatment for nerve pain and remote physical therapy. She says she fears returning to the high-security pod where she previously lived because she would be unable to defend herself if attacked.
 The settlement grew out of Pike’s lawsuit challenging years of isolation. It created an individualized plan that included work, shared meals, recreation and supervised group interaction. 
 The federal court dismissed the case after the agreement but retained jurisdiction to enforce it.
 Pike’s attorneys ask the judge to end her indefinite isolation and restore the plan to the fullest extent consistent with her medical needs and safety. They also seek attorneys’ fees and costs. The filing says the state opposes the requested relief.
 The judge has not yet ruled on the motion. FOX 17 News has reached out to TDOC for comment and has yet to hear back.
